lead.headline: This Congress passed 63 regular laws in its first 539 days, second-fewest since 2013; only the last Congress passed fewer
lead.number: 63 laws that aren't rule repeals, renamings or spending bills by day 539 of the 119th (builder said 67); the 113th-117th had 93-145 at the same point, the 118th 43.
lead.watch_out: "Regular law" is a title-keyword cut, not a classifier (it misses CRA votes titled "Disapproving the rule"); the fall 2025 shutdown (68 days with no laws) is an untested dull explanation.

According to the legislative tracking website GovTrack, the 119th Congress has passed just 27 bills, far fewer than many previous sessions since the 103rd Congress, which convened in 1993 when President Bill Clinton was in office. Since then, the least productive Congress in terms of laws passed was the 118th Congress, which had passed just 13 bills by a comparable stage of its session. This was largely due to Republicans controlling the House while Democrats controlled the Senate and the White House. There was also infighting in the Republican Party at the time which resulted in Kevin McCarthy losing his speakership, affecting Congress' ability to move legislation.
